clue.text: Way of moving packet over the radio

indicators.note: what comes over the radio is only heard, so the spelling is decided by sound alone

blocks.note: a sachet is a small sealed packet, as of sugar or shampoo

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a parcel can be sent by radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way of moving' looks like a description of delivering the packet, but it is the definition; the packet is a sachet, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk with a swaggering, swaying gait, so it is a particular manner of walking.

clue.text: School master key to zero sloppiness

blocks.note: SCH is the standard abbreviation for school
M is a recognised abbreviation for master
the Alt key on a computer keyboard
Z is a recognised abbreviation for zero

explanation.surface: A headmaster holds the key that leads to a slovenly school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master key' reads as one item, but it splits into M and a keyboard key, ALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality, the soppy, mawkish quality also called sloppiness in writing or music.

clue.text: Manager dropping by for new type of shade

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, and here a replacement is named to take its place

blocks.note: a supervisor manages staff
per means by, as in per post
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A boss swaps one kind of lampshade or blind for a novel design.
explanation.walkthrough: PER is taken out of SUPERVISOR and N is put in its place; 'for' marks the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun visor is a flap or peak that shields the eyes from glare, one particular kind of shade.

clue.text: Times in bottom of American pit

indicators.note: something placed in another thing ends up enclosed by it

blocks.note: by means times in multiplication, as in three by four
ass is the American word for the backside

explanation.surface: Times spent at the base of a US mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of American' looks like an instruction to take a last letter, but it means the American word for a bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm, so it is a very deep pit or hole in the ground.

clue.text: Sticking sacking across very loud instrument's head

indicators.note: the head of something is its front, so only the opening letter is wanted
something lying across another spans it on both sides, so it wraps around

blocks.note: axing is dismissing from a job
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
the first letter of instrument

explanation.surface: Hessian is being stuck over the end of a very noisy instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' suggests coarse hessian cloth in the surface, but it means dismissing someone from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Affixing means fastening or attaching one thing to another, which is what sticking does.

clue.text: Raffishly eccentric artist missing angle

indicators.note: something missing has been left out, so those letters are removed
something eccentric is off-centre and irregular, so these letters are put into an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A dashing, oddball painter is absent from a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: RA comes out of RAFFISHLY and the remaining seven letters are rearranged. 'Angle' looks like geometry but is the fishing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod and line, and fly-fishing is one particular method of doing so.

clue.text: I am on time and socially acceptable without any preparation

blocks.note: I am contracts to I'm
prompt means punctual
U means upper-class or socially acceptable, from the old U and non-U distinction

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being punctual and presentable despite doing no preparation at all.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U was a 1950s British label for upper-class versus lower-class usage, so U means socially acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done on the spur of the moment, unrehearsed and spontaneous.

clue.text: Grab osier, twisting segment into line

indicators.note: a segment is a section cut from something larger, so the letters come from within the words
twisting turns something round, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone seizes a willow stem and bends a piece into a straight row.
explanation.walkthrough: An osier is a willow whose shoots are used in basketry, which makes twisting it natural in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Comprehensive blog involved gangster

indicators.note: something involved is tangled and complicated, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A detailed online journal implicated a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' reads as 'implicated' in the surface, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Global can mean all-embracing or covering everything, as in a global view, which is comprehensive.

clue.text: Yanks in Ohio surrounded by unsophisticated people

indicators.note: whatever is surrounded is enclosed on all sides by the other piece

blocks.note: O is an old abbreviation for the US state of Ohio
hicks are country bumpkins

explanation.surface: Americans in Ohio are hemmed in by country folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' looks like Americans, fitting Ohio, but it is a verb meaning pulls sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoick is to lift or pull abruptly, so hoicks and yanks are both jerky tugging verbs.

clue.text: Marvellous, muscular fish

blocks.note: hunky means well built and muscular
a dory is a sea fish, as in John Dory

explanation.surface: Praise for a wonderfully strong fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes the two words look like a list of praise for one fish; the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for fine, satisfactory or excellent, close enough to marvellous.

clue.text: Flower concealing steamy picture

indicators.note: to conceal is to hide inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest river
steamy means hot

explanation.surface: A bloom hides a racy image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a bloom but is read as flow-er, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Raise rent for first house

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, meaning torn apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A landlord puts up the rent on someone's first home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment for housing, but it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: In astrology the zodiac is divided into twelve houses, and Aries is the first sign of the cycle.

clue.text: Leader of historic capital manoeuvring around old banger

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the first letter is taken
manoeuvring means moving things around into new positions
going around something encloses it

blocks.note: the first letter of historic
taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A historic city's ruler is shunting an old car about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old banger' looks like a clapped-out car; 'old' gives O and a banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, and banger is British slang for any sausage.

clue.text: Courageous men taking hearts of Cretans from Ajax and Thersites

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of each following word count

blocks.note: the centre letter of a seven-letter word
the two central letters of a four-letter word
the two central letters of a four-letter word
the centre letter of a three-letter word
the centre letter of a nine-letter word

explanation.surface: Brave warriors win over Greek heroes of the Iliad, Ajax and Thersites, alongside Cretans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts of' seems to cover only Cretans, but it applies to every word that follows, small linking words included.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is to toil heroically, since the defenders of Troy are proverbial for bravery and endurance.

clue.text: Parallel to a hypotenuse?

blocks.note: surface reading: running in the same direction as something, beside it
setter's reading: the hypotenuse is the longest edge of a right-angled triangle, and the three words describing it split the answer

explanation.surface: A geometry question about lines that run beside a triangle's slanting edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: read the answer as three words and it describes a hypotenuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside and level with, running next to something, which is what parallel to means.

clue.text: Smooth operator's secret desire

indicators.note: a secret is kept out of sight, so the letters are tucked inside other words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A charmer harbours a private longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret desire' reads as one phrase, but 'secret' is the signal and 'desire' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hope is a wish or longing for something to happen, a synonym of desire.

clue.text: Body parts, regularly skinned, play up

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, the opposite way

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
play means room to move, as in play in a rope

explanation.surface: Grazed limbs start to act up and give trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play up' looks like misbehaving, but it is play, meaning slack, turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecaps are the patellae, small bones at the front of each knee, so they are parts of the body.

clue.text: Divorcees covering writer's costs

indicators.note: to cover something is to go over and around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: divorced people are each other's exes
a pen is a writer, so writer's gives the plural-looking pen's

explanation.surface: Former spouses are paying an author's bills.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive writer's becomes pen's, and the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Expenses are money spent or outgoings, the same thing as costs.

clue.text: Shock line in note

indicators.note: a thing in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
to jot is to make a brief note

explanation.surface: A startling sentence turns up in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' sounds musical but is a jot, a brief written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A jolt is a sudden surprise or start, a shock to the system.

clue.text: Skill climbing say goes into flying act

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
say asks us to speak the word, so only its sound matters

blocks.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
goes is a euphemism for urinates

explanation.surface: An acrobat's talent rises as they head into an aerial routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but asks for a sound, and 'goes' is the euphemism for relieving oneself; the last syllable sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The trapeze is the swinging bar used by circus aerialists, and the term stands for their high-flying performance.

clue.text: French who rejected working within old twelve-hour day

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run backwards
within means inside, so these pieces are enclosed

blocks.note: qui is French for who
on means working or operating, as a machine is on
ex means former

explanation.surface: An old French regime refused work during a short shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like it describes the day but gives EX, which wraps around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: At an equinox day and night are each roughly twelve hours long, so the daylight lasts half the clock.

clue.text: Grant immunity to European politician replacing one in withdrawal

indicators.note: replacing means taking the place of, so one letter is swapped out for another piece

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
an MP is a Member of Parliament
the Roman numeral for one
an exit is a departure

explanation.surface: A Euro-politician is shielded from prosecution when stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: EMP takes the place of I in EXIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from an obligation or liability, which is giving them immunity.

clue.text: Vanquishes most terrible things

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, defeats or gets the better of
second meaning: a plural noun, the very poorest examples

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is old-fashioned but current: to worst an opponent is to beat them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning defeats and as a plural noun for the worst examples of anything.

clue.text: Familiar sensation of French getting German agreement to rising radiation

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising goes upwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: de is French for of
ja is German for yes
UV is ultraviolet radiation

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and a German sign a treaty on increasing nuclear radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself French, so the French and German pieces fit the surface naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Deja vu is the uncanny feeling of having experienced the present moment before, a sense of familiarity.

clue.text: Misuse field in part of match, beginning to get level

indicators.note: the beginning is the start, so only the first letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end
the first letter of get
to raze a building is to level it to the ground

explanation.surface: A player abuses a field in part of a game to get the scores level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' and 'match' suggest sport, but the field is pasture and the match is cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To overgraze is to let livestock eat pasture so heavily that the land is damaged, an abuse of grassland.

clue.text: European got married in Greater London area

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: to wed is to marry
SE is the south-east London postcode area

explanation.surface: A continental visitor ties the knot in the London suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: London postcodes such as SE, SW and NW are often used as abbreviations for areas of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, so a person from Europe.

clue.text: Baby bird born under illegally occupied building with no foundation

indicators.note: without a foundation the base is gone, and in a down entry the base is the final letter
in a down entry, a piece placed under another comes after it

blocks.note: b is the abbreviation for born
a squat is a building taken over without permission

explanation.surface: A chick is hatched beneath an unsafe, unlawfully occupied building.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the foundation of SQUAT is its last letter, and B goes beneath what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A squab is a young pigeon not yet fledged, so it is a baby bird.

clue.text: Took to the water with independent teacher

blocks.note: took to the water means went for a swim, in the past tense
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A private-school tutor went for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent teacher' reads as a private tutor, but 'independent' is just I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man, often addressed as a spiritual guide.

clue.text: Sixth sense over America and Latin States' final unions

indicators.note: final means last, so only the end letter is wanted

blocks.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the sixth sense
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
the United States of America
L is the abbreviation for Latin
the last letter of States

explanation.surface: A psychic foresees the eventual alliances of the US and Latin American nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America and Latin States' wants to be Latin America; the words split into separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousals are marriages or betrothals, the formal joining of two people in union.

clue.text: Something to mop up geese flying over Quebec

indicators.note: flying things scatter in all directions, so these letters are rearranged
to fly over is to pass across from one side to the other, so one piece spans the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Que. is an abbreviation for the Canadian province of Quebec

explanation.surface: Migrating geese pass over Canada, and something must clean up after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mop up' sounds like it is the action; the whole phrase 'Something to mop up' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeegee is a rubber-edged blade on a handle used to wipe liquid off windows and floors.

clue.text: Exploits of Australian coaches

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for Australian
a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: Adventures of sports coaches from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploits' looks like a noun for adventures, but it works as a verb; 'coaches' looks like trainers but is vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse someone is to take unfair advantage of them, which is what exploiting means.
